subject: Hosted commit sprint: Cartwell onramp & pro-rata burst
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Tuttle <sam.tuttle@cartwell.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted commit sprint: Cartwell onramp & pro-rata burst

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. Based on the usage profile you shared, I sketched a staged commit that gives Cartwell predictable unit economics for high-volume inference while leaving headroom for seasonal spikes. Key ideas: a higher monthly commit (to lower per-token price), a small pro-rata bridge for the first partial month, and a defined burst bucket you can draw against without latency penalties.

Quick ask: can you confirm (A) the 3‑month onboarding window you mentioned, and (B) whether accounting needs invoices on a monthly calendar or a 30‑day rolling window? I want to align billing and the kickoff date.

I attached the Q1 usage export you shared (reformatted) so we can annotate the ramp tiers. If you want, I can loop in Ben for pricing and Marissa for onboarding ops.

Attachment: Cartwell_Usage_Q1_2027.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 415‑555‑0148

From: Sam Tuttle <sam.tuttle@cartwell.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted commit sprint: Cartwell onramp & pro-rata burst

Kim —

Appreciate the summary. Yes to the 3‑month onboarding window; that lines up with our internal launch plan. For billing, finance prefers calendar‑month invoices but can accept a 30‑day cycle if it simplifies implementation. Two follow-ups:

1) Can you map the proposed tiers to the specific endpoints we'll hit (generation vs. embeddings)? We need to validate the expected token mix.
2) For the burst bucket — what gating/soft‑throttle behavior should we expect if we exceed it during promo events? We want to avoid throttled customer-facing requests.

If you can include Ben and Marissa on the next thread that'd be great.

— Sam
Sam Tuttle
Head of Product, Cartwell Inc
sam.tuttle@cartwell.com | +1 212‑555‑0199

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sam Tuttle <sam.tuttle@cartwell.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cartwell.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted commit sprint: Cartwell onramp & pro-rata burst

Ben / Marissa — looping you in to scope pricing and the onboarding checklist. Sam confirmed a 3‑month onboarding window and preference for calendar‑month invoices (flexible).

Sam — Ben drafted a few tier pairings that balance generation/embedding mix and gives you a soft burst cushion. Marissa will outline the operational kickoff timeline and what telemetry we need to lock low‑latency SLOs during promotions.

Ben — can you take point on: (1) a two‑tier commit plan (Base monthly commit + Seasonal burst bucket), (2) a pro‑rata charge for the initial partial month, and (3) suggested per‑token rates for generation / embedding mix (assume 80/20 gen/emb for forecast). Also add a note on soft‑throttle behavior and automatic fallback to a compatible lower-cost variant if latency SLOs would otherwise be breached.

Marissa — please include the onboarding milestones (test harness, eval set pass, traffic mirroring window, GA cutover) and any dependencies on customer security signoffs.

Thanks — Sam, Lena, you'll see a formal SOW + pricing note from Ben shortly.

Best,
Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Tuttle <sam.tuttle@cartwell.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hosted commit sprint: Cartwell onramp & pro-rata burst

Hi team — attaching a draft SOW + pricing grid for Cartwell. High level proposal:

- Base commit: 6.5M tokens/month (12‑month term) at $0.0009 / gen‑token, $0.0004 / emb‑unit (assumes quantized model family).
- Seasonal burst pocket: 1.5M tokens usable per month for 3 months of the year (pro‑rated on first month).
- Pro‑rata: first partial month billed on calendar days used; we can lock kickoff to first of next month if Cartwell prefers no pro‑rata.
- Soft‑throttle & fallbacks: primary routing keeps requests on the pinned model; when burst is exhausted we will route new requests to a compatible lower‑cost variant with automated quality monitoring and an alert to both CS and Cartwell. Latency SLA: 95th pct <= 180ms for generation (within Redwood Dedicated targets); if we cannot meet latency during sustained overload, we fall back and notify.

Attachments: SOW_Cartwell_Commit_2027_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Related: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/4721 (deal record)

If that looks good I can send a cleaned SOW + signature link (DocuSign) and Marissa will begin onboarding planning.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650‑555‑0122

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cartwell.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sam Tuttle <sam.tuttle@cartwell.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted commit sprint: Cartwell onramp & pro-rata burst

Thanks — the numbers look reasonable. Two quick notes from finance/legal: (1) please include a 30‑day payment term on invoices, and (2) we need a short clause clarifying data retention for cached prefixes used in KV caching. Can you add those to the SOW? Otherwise we can sign next week.

Sam and I are aligned on proceeding — can you send the DocuSign link once the SOW is updated?

Best,
Lena Ortiz
VP Finance, Cartwell Inc
lena.ortiz@cartwell.com | +1 212‑555‑0111
